convention: RED's own Recording Time tool (reddigitalcinema.com/tools, data file tools-20250813.json, Svelte source in cms.reddigitalcinema.com/.../tools.frag.html) computes: data rate MB/s = W x H x factor/8 x fps / ratio / 1e6 (x2 with HDRx/Extended Highlights), with factor = 14 bits/photosite for all DRAGON, HELIUM, GEMINI, MONSTRO, KOMODO and V-RAPTOR cameras and 12 for SCARLET MYSTERIUM-X / RED ONE. So REDCODE ratio is relative to 14-bit raw: bpp = 14/ratio (12/ratio for Mysterium-X), NOT 16/ratio. Record time in the tool adds 5% overhead (rate x 1.05) and treats GB as 1024 MB (KOMODO: 1000). Verification 1 (DSMC3 presets = fixed ratios HQ 3.5:1, MQ 5:1, LQ 8:1, ELQ 11-15:1 by resolution): RED V-RAPTOR [X] guide 8K 17:9 24P HQ 425 MB/s; model 8192*4320*14/8*24/1e6/3.5 = 424.7 MB/s; MQ 298 (297.3), LQ 186 (185.8), ELQ 100 (99.1 at 15:1); 6K 17:9 24P 239/168/105/65 = 238.9/167.2/104.5/64.3(13:1). V-RAPTOR XL guide prints the same x1.05 (446/312/195/104). Verification 2 (DSMC2 ratios): DSMC2 MONSTRO/HELIUM spec min REDCODE at 300 MB/s media: 8K FF 24fps 5:1, 60fps 12:1, 4K FF 24fps 2:1, 60fps 3:1 -> 14-bit model needs 4.72, 11.8, 1.18, 2.95 (ceil = 5,12,2,3 exactly, treating 300 MB/s as MiB/s); 16-bit would give 6:1 at 8K24. EPIC DRAGON 6K FF 24fps 4:1 / 60fps 10:1 at 200 MB/s also matches 14-bit. 8K 24fps 5:1 example: 297.3 MB/s = 2378 Mb/s, bpp 2.8. Real R3D files are VBR and average around (often slightly below) these nominal values.
